column3: rationale
Closed breakdowns produce exact restoration and completed part-lead percentiles
Unreceived required part and absent verification remain open rather than zero duration
Breakdown requires explicit failure detection
Weather/site-access interruption cannot be misclassified as machine repair
Part received must follow a recorded part order
Repair work requires a diagnosis-complete timestamp
Repair completion cannot exist without repair start
Machine restoration requires recorded repair completion
Availability verification requires service-restored event
No event may be after the as-of boundary
Event chronology must be monotone
Repair episode IDs must be unique
Every affected request must join to canonical service-access identity
An affected request cannot be duplicated within one episode
Repair and canonical service-access scopes must match
Repair and canonical service-access periods must match
Repair event currency must match the declared assessment
Asset configuration identity is required
Stale repair event evidence blocks the summary
Malformed evidence digest shape blocks
Source references preserve provenance but do not authenticate artifacts
Partial-log declaration remains visible in output
Empty partial log does not imply zero real-world incidents
Weather interruption duration remains separate from repair restore time
Scheduled maintenance cannot inflate breakdown count
A required part must have a timestamp
Repair cannot start while a declared required part is absent
Exact event timestamps remain decimal strings for JSON consumers
